newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Coffee likely to challenge resistance.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Coffee likely to challenge resistance.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40
Coffee is more likely to attack resistance and head upwards than fall, technical analysts said.
Traders called it to open $15 higher.
Resistance at $1,675 will probably be challenged, Elli Gifford, an independent technical analyst, said. "It were taken out the move could extend to $1,800."
"A lot depends on support at $1,580 holding," she said. "I think it will."
"It's more likely to go up than down," Gifford said.
New York coffee futures rose sharply on Monday, bolstered by keen local and speculative buying amid persistent concerns about a near-term shortage of quality supply, traders said.
Hot weather caused by the El Nino effect could lead to a deterioration in the quality of Colombian coffee in the 1997/98 cycle, experts said Monday.

But the phenomenon, which meteorologists say will bring exceptionally hot, dry spells to part of Colombia and unseasonal, torrential rains to other areas, is unlikely to affect the volume of the crop, coffee experts said.
Colombia will open registrations for September coffee exports next week once all August export commitments are fulfilled, the head of the National Coffee Growers' Federation said on Monday.
Peru's non-decaffeinated coffee exports rose to $162 million in the first half of the year, up 104 percent compared with the same period in 1996, customs officials said Monday.
Mexico exported 148,009 60-kg bags of coffee in June compared to the 193,292 bags in June last year, the Mexican Coffee Council said Monday.
Indian Commerce Minister Bolla Buli Ramaiah was quoted on Tuesday as saying there was no need to allow coffee imports as prices have come down from recent peaks.
"There is absolutely no need for import of coffee as the prices are under control," the Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Ramaiah as saying in an interview in the capital New Delhi.
